short: The document used when no GST can be charged on a supply.
seoTitle: Bill of Supply — Meaning and Example for Businesses
metaDescription: The document used when no GST can be charged on a supply. It carries no tax amount and confers no input tax credit. Part of the free Setu business glossary.
definition: A bill of supply is issued instead of a tax invoice when a supplier cannot charge GST — typically a composition dealer, or a supply of exempt goods and services. It carries no tax amount and confers no input tax credit.
bodyHtml:
Why Bill of Supply matters

Using a tax invoice where a bill of supply is required, or the reverse, misstates the tax position on the face of the document and confuses customers who try to claim credit from it.

How Bill of Supply works in practice

Keep a separate document series for bills of supply so the two never share numbering. A composition dealer's bill of supply must also declare that the supplier is not eligible to collect tax on supplies.

faq.question: Can a customer claim credit from a bill of supply?
faq.answer: No. No tax is charged on it, so there is nothing to claim.

faq.question: When do exempt goods need a bill of supply?
faq.answer: Whenever a registered person supplies exempt or nil-rated goods or services, in place of a tax invoice.
